## TL;DR

The task drawer now gives a fresh close-out failure precedence over an older waiting or review status, and it no longer shows the separate waiting banner at the same time. The duplicate information popover was removed, the failure heading now says “Close-out failed,” and the detailed error card uses the drawer’s standard 22-pixel side gutter and 8-pixel vertical margin. The drawer elapsed-time display now uses the shared `useNow` clock, so opening the drawer does not leave its timer dependent on a running check poll loop.

## Work and rationale

The failure state had two sources of status UI: the dedicated `DoneErrorCard` for a failed Move to done operation, and the regular critical waiting banner for the older needs-input state. The general drawer summary already used `selectDrawerStatus`, but the detailed error and waiting elements sat outside that summary’s exclusive slot. I made `handoffFailed` the first candidate in the selector so fresh failures are chosen before waiting and review conditions. The dedicated error component remains responsible for presenting full failure output and actions. When it is present, the normal actionable waiting banner is suppressed, including the questions banner path, so only one status card remains visible.

The detailed failure panel already contains the check output and retry/debug actions. Its information icon opened a small popover that restated failure guidance and sat in the same visual region as output. I removed that popover and its icon. The headline now identifies the failure plainly as “Close-out failed.” The embedded panel is constrained to the same horizontal gutter as other drawer content and has a matching vertical margin, keeping its edges and gaps aligned.

For elapsed time, the drawer had a separate one-second timer started only when the check loop started. That could stop reflecting time during handoff transitions or while polling changed state. I changed the drawer’s `checkNow` source to `useNow`, the composable used for shared once-a-second live time updates, and removed the redundant timer lifecycle. The drawer’s check heading continues to use the same `formatChecksCardLine` helper as the task card, preserving step wording such as “checking review.”

Regression coverage adds a priority case proving handoff failure wins over both waiting and review failure candidates. A rendered TaskDrawer test seeds a stale needs-input state and a current close-out error and verifies that only the close-out card appears, its headline is clear, no help popover exists, and check output remains readable. Existing priority tests continue to cover the other status orderings.

## Approaches tried

I first traced the rendered status region and found that changing the priority selector alone could not remove the second card because the waiting banner and detailed error panel were independent template branches. I then applied the priority update and added suppression at the actual waiting-card visibility boundary, with an explicit guard on the questions banner. This keeps the selector deterministic while addressing both independent render paths.

I initially added a second `useNow` import while editing the clock, but the component already imported it for other live timestamps. The focused test run caught the duplicate declaration immediately; I removed the duplicate and reran the tests. The test also showed that this store exposes `doneErrors` as state rather than a public `setDoneError` action, so the fixture now seeds the store state in the same style as the existing tests.

## Challenges and blockers

The main challenge was identifying the boundaries of “one status card.” The prioritized summary, dedicated close-out error card, and waiting/needs-input banner have distinct rendering paths. The fix keeps the detailed error component because it owns useful output and actions, and makes the older waiting card yield whenever the current failure is present.

No external account, device, or human action was required. The requested source changes do not touch `repoos.toml`, task metadata, or generated build output. The final required scoped RepoOS check passed: all 64 changed-path test files (617 tests), the always-run boot timing test, UI smoke, formatting, lint, contrast, and other applicable local guards completed successfully. An earlier full-suite attempt through `repoos check --fix` passed 705 of 708 test files but encountered three unrelated failures in debugger integration, pressure-guard timing, and remote-host lock timing on the remote runner; the scoped check on the final tree passed.

## Key learnings

A centralized priority model only guarantees a single visible status if every status surface participates in the same decision or explicitly yields to the selected higher-priority state. Dedicated error panels need to be included in that audit even when they are not part of the summary component.

Live elapsed displays should use a clock whose lifecycle matches the visible consumer. Tying the drawer’s display clock to a polling loop makes it vulnerable to state transitions that stop or restart polling. Using the shared clock keeps the displayed age live independently of check-row refresh cadence.
